Native era-selection reconstruction, DF 53.16 Windows
===================================================

These are source-inspection notes, not executable code or a test. Function and
field names are reconstructed with data/upstream/df-structures/df.history.xml,
df.history_figure.xml, df.creature.xml, and df.region.xml. The original game is
closed source; the stored .asm files are the actual static PE disassembly.

Images inspected:
reference: D:/program/steam/steamapps/common/Dwarf Fortress/Dwarf Fortress.exe
           PE:6a70a6d9:02711000
classic:   C:/Users/WIN11/Downloads/df_53_16_win/Dwarf Fortress.exe
           PE:6a70b91c:0270a000
Image base: 0x140000000 for both. Addresses below are RVAs.

Role                        reference range       classic range
build era determiner        bb7060..bb74ff         bb40a0..bb453f
choose era type             bb7500..bb7799         bb4540..bb47d9
create initial era          bb77a0..bb7b75         bb47e0..bb4bb5
update era and ordinals     bb8910..bb8e02         bb5950..bb5e42

Era enum, signed int16_t:
  -1 NONE; 0 ThreePowers; 1 TwoPowers; 2 OnePower; 3 Myth; 4 Legends;
   5 Twilight; 6 FairyTales; 7 Race (RACE_DOMINANT); 8 Heroes;
   9 Golden; 10 Death; 11 Civilization; 12 Emptiness.

Determiner offsets:
  +00 living_powers; +04 living_megabeasts; +08 living_semimegabeasts
  +0c/+10/+14 first three POWER/MEGABEAST/TITAN historical-figure IDs
  +18 vector<int32> civilized counts by creature race
  +30 civilized_total; +34 civilized_mundane

Title offsets (era_infost):
  +00 type; +04/+08 histfig IDs or dominant race index; +0c ordinal
  +10 translated_name (string); +30 percent

Build determiner (reference bb7060):
  zero counts; initialize power_hf[0..2] to -1
  for hf in world.history.figures:
    if hf.flags.DEITY or hf.flags.FORCE: continue
    if hf.died_year != -1: continue
    if hf.caste.flags.POWER:
      ++living_powers; store hf.id if fewer than three IDs stored
    else if hf.caste.flags.MEGABEAST or hf.caste.flags.TITAN:
      ++living_megabeasts; store hf.id if fewer than three IDs stored
    else if hf.caste.flags.SEMIMEGABEAST:
      ++living_semimegabeasts
    if hf.civ_id != -1 and hf.race is a valid race index:
      ++civilized_races[hf.race]; ++civilized_total
      if hf.race.flags.MUNDANE: ++civilized_mundane
  for pop in world.entity_populations:
    if not pop.flags.all_local_links: continue
    for paired (race, count) in pop.races/pop.counts:
      if race is valid:
        civilized_races[race] += count; civilized_total += count
        if race.flags.MUNDANE: civilized_mundane += count

Flag mappings from current df-structures, matched to native flag tests:
  caste POWER=124 (byte15 bit4), MEGABEAST=110 (byte13 bit6),
  SEMIMEGABEAST=111 (byte13 bit7), TITAN=132 (byte16 bit4).
  FEATURE_BEAST=131, UNIQUE_DEMON=133, DEMON=134 are not separately counted
  in this routine; a creature can qualify through the counted flags above.
  creature MUNDANE=2 (byte0 bit2).
  historical-figure DEITY=2/FORCE=3 are skipped; died_year is hf+30.
  entity_population all_local_links=bit0, read from pop+e4.

Initial-era routine (reference bb77a0):
  initial_mega_power_sum is calculated as the number of living historical
  figures whose caste has POWER or MEGABEAST or TITAN; skips DEITY/FORCE.
  Its address in this reference PE is 0x1424f9f44.
  It creates an era with start_year=-1, computes a determiner, calls the
  selector and the separate title formatter, and appends it to history.eras.

Choose era (reference bb7500):
  out = {NONE, index1=-1, index2=-1, ordinal=0, name="", percent=0}
  G = living_powers + living_megabeasts
  B = world.history.initial_mega_power_sum

  if B <= 3:
    if G > 3: return Myth
    if G == 3: return ThreePowers
    if G == 2 and power_hf[0] != -1 and power_hf[1] != -1:
      return TwoPowers, index1=power_hf[0], index2=power_hf[1]
    if G == 1 and power_hf[0] != -1:
      return OnePower, index1=power_hf[0]
  else:
    if G >= integer_truncate((2 * B) / 3): return Myth
    if G >= integer_truncate(B / 3): return Legends
    if G > 0: return Heroes

  max_race_count, max_race = maximum positive civilized_races element
  if max_race valid and max_race_count > 0 and civilized_total > 0:
    mundane_percent = integer_truncate(100 * civilized_mundane / civilized_total)
    if mundane_percent >= 50:
      out.percent = mundane_percent
      if mundane_percent < 90: return Twilight
      if living_powers + living_megabeasts + living_semimegabeasts == 0
          and civilized_mundane == civilized_total:
        return Civilization
      return FairyTales
    dominant_percent = integer_truncate(100 * max_race_count / civilized_total)
    if dominant_percent >= 50:
      return Race, index1=max_race, percent=dominant_percent
    return Golden

  for old_era in history.eras, newest first:
    if old_era.type in {Twilight, FairyTales, Race, Golden, Civilization}:
      return Death
  return Emptiness

Important source distinctions:
  * Heroes has no G>3 condition when B>3. It is the remaining positive range
    below integer_truncate(B/3), so the common wiki >3 simplification is not
    the exact condition in these installed images.
  * Three/Two/OnePowers branches are selected only when B<=3 (with the G>3
    fallback to Myth). They are not universal later phases of a large world.
  * MUNDANE is an explicit creature flag. The percentage is not population
    of all civilization races, and not a technological progress measurement.
  * Golden is a demographics fallback. The selector does not count peace,
    prosperity, wealth, happiness, or legendary heroes.
  * Death remembers that a demographic civilization-era once existed.
    Emptiness uses the same current absence of counted civilization when
    no prior era in that set exists. Neither means no animal life remains.

Era update (reference bb8910):
  if history.eras empty: create initial era; return
  current = history.eras.back()
  candidate = choose_era(build_determiner())
  same_key(a,b) = a.type==b.type and a.index1==b.index1 and a.index2==b.index2

  if candidate.type in {Twilight, FairyTales, Race, Civilization}
      and not same_key(current,candidate) and candidate.percent < 60:
    candidate.type = Golden
    candidate.index1 = candidate.index2 = -1
  if same_key(current,candidate): return

  append new era at current game year, including full determiner and title info
  occurrence_count = 0
  for old_era before this newly appended era, chronological order:
    if same_key(old_era,candidate):
      ++occurrence_count
      old_era.ordinal = occurrence_count
      if occurrence_count == 1:
        new_era.translated_name = old_era.translated_name
  if occurrence_count > 0:
    new_era.ordinal = occurrence_count + 1
  else:
    format new era base title

The 60% update gate means an existing Twilight/Race era can continue at
50..59%, while a different Twilight/Race key needs 60% to begin; the initial
era bypasses this update gate. FairyTales (>=90%) and Civilization (=100%)
already exceed it. Ordinals count recurrence of the same type and both title
indices, not the world's overall era index; prior first occurrences become
numbered retroactively. The separate display routine adds ordinal wording.

Golden must therefore be described with both routes: the selector's no-dominant
race demographic fallback, and the updater's below-60% new-Twilight/new-Race
fallback. Describing Golden only as MUNDANE<50% and no race>=50% would omit the
second route, including cases where MUNDANE or a dominant race is at 50..59%.

Monster / Rampage belong to a historical-event collection title
------------------------------------------------------------

Static reads from the same current reference PE:
  beast-attack collection vtable RVA 1626180, slot +00 -> RVA 67b90
  RVA 67b90: mov eax,6; ret
  same vtable, slot +30 (getName) -> RVA bc6880
  title formatter function RVA bc6880..bc6b9c
  at RVA bc6a67: literal RVA 16c2058, "Monster"
  at RVA bc6a8e: literal RVA 16dfad0, "Rampage"
  complete annotated source: reference-beast-attack-collection-title.asm

The mapping to history_event_collection_beast_attackst is corroborated by
data/extracted/statue-history-sources.tsv rows concrete_rtti/root for that
class and by data/upstream/df-structures/df.history_collection.xml:
  history_event_collection_type: NONE=-1, WAR=0 ... BEAST_ATTACK=6 ...
  ENTITY_OVERTHROWN=17 (18 actual collection types).
  beast attack fields include parent collection, region/layer/site,
  defender civilization, attacker historical-figure list, and ordinal.

Native title reconstruction:
  "The " + optional collection ordinal + " "
  if attacker_hf.size() > 1:
    race = common_attacker_race(collection)  // helper RVA bc6780
    if race == -1: append "Monster"
    else: append capitalized creature_raw.name[2] (adjective at +60)
    append " "
  append "Rampage"
  if attacker_hf.size() == 1: append " of " + historical-figure name
  append " in " + site, region, or "the Wilds"

Thus "The [ordinal] Monster Rampage in ..." and "The [ordinal] Rampage of ..."
are names of beast-attack historical-event collections, not era names. This
conclusion does not rely on mere string proximity: the PE vtable getType=6,
getName slot, title body, and separate collection enum establish the owner.
The era selector and era title switch use the 13 era_type values 0..12; their
Powers variants are a different naming family. Shared ordinal wording must
not cause these families to be conflated.
